# Staticseal

> Create a standalone HTML package from a file, report or static website. Recipients open it in a browser, optionally with a passphrase. The browser creator processes files locally without an upload, account or backend.

## Choose a local tool

- Browser creator: download only [staticseal.html](https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/releases/latest/download/staticseal.html). Version 2.0.0 is 61,613 bytes (about 62 kB / 60 KiB). It contains its runtime dependencies and works offline; no Node.js or npm installation is needed. This size describes the creator, not the CLI checkout or the resulting packages.
- CLI automation: download or clone the repository. The entry point is `bin/self-encrypt.mjs`; it imports `bin/lib/` and `src/`, including checked-in generated reader modules. Downloading the entry script alone is insufficient. No build is required to run the CLI from a release checkout.
- Single file or self-contained HTML: the CLI needs only a supported Node.js runtime and the checkout; no npm dependencies are required when `--bundle` is absent.
- HTML/MHTML report with separate resources: use CLI `--bundle` after `npm ci --omit=dev`. This installs the runtime dependencies, including Happy DOM, without development tools.
- Multiple independent files or a website with linked HTML subpages: use the browser creator's file/folder selection. The CLI does not create multi-file collections or crawl hyperlinks to subpages. Do not pass a directory as `--in`.

## CLI setup

Use Node.js 24 LTS, or a supported Node.js 20.x (20.19+) or 22.x (22.13+) release; the repository's `package.json` engines field defines the exact range. With Node.js and npm installed, run these commands in a new working directory to install the documented 2.0.0 release without Git or development tools:

```sh
curl -fL https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/archive/refs/tags/v2.0.0.tar.gz -o staticseal-2.0.0.tar.gz
tar -xzf staticseal-2.0.0.tar.gz
cd staticseal-2.0.0
npm ci --omit=dev
node bin/self-encrypt.mjs --version
node bin/self-encrypt.mjs --help
```

No build is needed. `npm ci --omit=dev` installs only runtime dependencies; skip it if you will not use `--bundle`. Alternatively, clone the source with `git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.0.0 https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal.git` and run the same Node/npm commands inside the checkout. The repository is not published as an npm package. Do not assume `npx self-encrypt` installs this project.

## Non-interactive recipes

Replace the absolute paths below with the user's input and intended output. Select a new output path: a successful command overwrites an existing output file. Always specify `--no-password` or `--stdin-password` in automation; otherwise the CLI prompts interactively.

Package one file without encryption:

```sh
node bin/self-encrypt.mjs --in /path/to/report.pdf --out /path/to/report.sealed.html --no-password
```

Display already self-contained HTML as a webpage, preserving its input bytes:

```sh
node bin/self-encrypt.mjs --in /path/to/report.html --out /path/to/report.sealed.html --html-page --no-password
```

Bundle a report folder by naming its HTML entry file, not the folder:

```sh
node bin/self-encrypt.mjs --in /path/to/report/index.html --out /path/to/report.sealed.html --bundle --no-password
```

`--bundle` implies `--html-page` and embeds supported referenced resources, not every file in the folder. It does not crawl linked HTML subpages. For resource roots, HTTP inputs, MHTML and unsupported dependencies, see the [CLI reference](https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/blob/main/docs/cli.md).

Protect a report using a user-provided passphrase via standard input:

```sh
node bin/self-encrypt.mjs --in /path/to/report/index.html --out /path/to/report.sealed.html --bundle --stdin-password < /path/to/passphrase.txt
```

Use an existing protected secret source or pipe the passphrase through the process's stdin. Do not put the passphrase in command arguments, logs or public titles. `--stdin-password` removes one trailing line ending and rejects an empty passphrase. `--no-password` provides no confidentiality.

## Verify the result and explain limits

- Require exit code 0 and the expected output file. The CLI verifies the payload roundtrip before writing; a successful exit does not prove that a bundled report is fully offline or visually correct.
- Inspect stderr for import warnings. Missing or unsupported resources may remain as original URLs even after a successful command. Open the result offline and check images, styling, navigation and interactions before claiming it is self-contained.
- Sources and prepared content are limited to 128 MiB; the final HTML package is limited to 25 MiB. These are file-size limits, not peak-memory guarantees.
- `--html-page` and `--bundle` outputs execute imported HTML/JavaScript when opened. Use trusted input. Bundling does not execute scripts during capture, automate login or bundle JavaScript module graphs.
- Browser website packages support ordinary internal navigation and Back. Modifier-click, middle-click and new-tab navigation to embedded subpages have known limitations.
- Give the user the output path and whether the package is encrypted. Packaging does not itself upload or publish the result.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/blob/main/README.md): browser quick start, protection and limits.
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/blob/main/docs/cli.md): full options, supported imports and reporting workflows.
- [Examples](https://nox-do.github.io/staticseal/examples/): file collections, HTML websites, PDFs and reporting workflows.
- [CLI examples](https://nox-do.github.io/staticseal/examples/cli/): Jupyter and Python-report recipes.
- [Releases](https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/releases): standalone browser download and source archives.
- [Development](https://github.com/nox-do/staticseal/blob/main/docs/development.md): architecture, generated files, builds and tests; development requires the full `npm ci` installation.
